text: [p01] Halvorsen Freight Systems is a fictional logistics company headquartered in Bergen, Norway. It operates refrigerated trucking, port terminal services and a freight software business. This report covers fiscal 2025, which ended on December 31, 2025.
[p02] Total revenue was NOK 9,412 million in fiscal 2025, compared with NOK 8,736 million in fiscal 2024. The increase came mainly from new cold-chain contracts with grocery retailers.
[p03] Refrigerated trucking revenue was NOK 5,980 million in fiscal 2025. Port terminal services revenue was NOK 2,614 million, and freight software revenue was NOK 818 million.
[p04] Freight software revenue grew 31% in fiscal 2025. Recurring subscription revenue accounted for 74% of freight software revenue.
[p05] Operating profit (EBIT) was NOK 1,047 million in fiscal 2025, compared with NOK 912 million in fiscal 2024. The operating margin was 11.1%.
[p06] Net income attributable to shareholders was NOK 688 million in fiscal 2025. Earnings per share were NOK 4.12, up from NOK 3.57 in fiscal 2024.
[p07] Fuel costs were NOK 1,893 million in fiscal 2025, down 6% from the prior year, as the company replaced 140 diesel trucks with battery-electric models.
[p08] At year-end 2025 the trucking fleet consisted of 1,260 vehicles, of which 310 were battery-electric. At year-end 2024 the fleet had 1,205 vehicles, of which 170 were battery-electric.
[p09] Capital expenditure was NOK 1,322 million in fiscal 2025. About half went to fleet electrification and the rest to terminal cranes and IT systems.
[p10] The company employed 6,840 people at the end of 2025, up from 6,515 a year earlier. Employee turnover among drivers fell to 14.2% from 17.9%.
[p11] The Stavanger port terminal handled 412,000 containers (TEU) in 2025, a record. Average crane productivity was 27 moves per hour.
[p12] Net interest-bearing debt was NOK 3,105 million at December 31, 2025, equal to 1.9 times EBITDA. The company's revolving credit facility of NOK 2,000 million was undrawn.
[p13] Cash flow from operations was NOK 1,604 million in fiscal 2025. Free cash flow, after capital expenditure, was NOK 282 million.
[p14] The board proposes a dividend of NOK 1.80 per share for fiscal 2025, compared with NOK 1.50 for fiscal 2024.
[p15] On-time delivery for refrigerated trucking was 96.4% in 2025. Temperature excursions, where cargo left its required range, occurred on 0.3% of shipments.
[p16] Scope 1 greenhouse gas emissions were 182,000 tonnes of CO2 equivalent in 2025, a reduction of 9% from 2024. The company targets a 50% reduction from its 2022 baseline by 2030.
[p17] The largest customer, a Nordic grocery chain, accounted for 12% of total revenue. No other customer exceeded 5%.
[p18] In March 2025 Halvorsen acquired Kystlink AS, a coastal shipping planner, for NOK 240 million. Kystlink contributed NOK 96 million of revenue after the acquisition.
[p19] For fiscal 2026 management expects revenue growth of 5% to 7% and an operating margin between 11% and 12%.
[p20] Principal risks include fuel and electricity price volatility, driver availability, port labour negotiations and the pace of customer adoption of the freight software platform.
[p21] The freight software platform had 1,930 business customers at year-end 2025, compared with 1,410 at year-end 2024.
[p22] Lost-time injury frequency was 3.1 per million hours worked in 2025, compared with 3.8 in 2024.
[p23] The company's chief executive is Ingrid Solheim, who has led Halvorsen since 2019. The board has seven members, three of whom are independent.
[p24] Halvorsen's shares are listed on the Oslo stock exchange. There were 167 million shares outstanding at year-end 2025.
